transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's very nice to meet you, too. Um... well, I guess I'm here because of a little issue at work. I work as a cashier, and... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I keep getting sort of stuck doing things that don't really fit the moment. 

Like, I'll just be at the register and I'll start tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or... or I'll just kind of freeze with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while a customer is waiting. I really don't mean to do it, I promise, and I always try to be a good employee. But it actually got me written up last week, which makes me feel awful. I just want to fix whatever is going wrong so I don't cause any more trouble at the store. Does that make sense? Is that the right kind of thing to come here for?
When you get stuck like that, does it feel like you have to do it to relieve an uncomfortable thought or a 'not right' feeling?

Oh, um... no, I don't think it's quite like that. I hope I'm explaining this right, but I don't really have a bad thought or a 'not right' feeling I'm trying to get rid of. It's not like I'm doing it on purpose to make myself feel better. 

It's more like... I just sort of blank out for a second, or my hand just does the tapping on its own. I don't feel anxious or anything right before it happens, I just kind of... get stuck. Is that... does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so we can figure this out. I really don't want to be a difficult patient.
When the tapping or freezing happens, does it feel completely involuntary, like your body does it by itself even when you try not to?

Well, yes, I suppose it is involuntary. I mean, I definitely wouldn't choose to do it, especially with a line of people waiting! 

Like I was mentioning earlier, with the tapping or when my hand just hovers over the open drawer... I'm just trying to ring the person up, and it's like I just pause. It's really just a tiny little glitch, you know? Nothing too crazy. I wouldn't even bother you with it, honestly, because I can usually just shake it off after a moment. But since it got me written up last week, I figured I better get it sorted out so my manager is happy. I really am a hard worker, I promise. 

Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm making sense. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
Right before the tapping happens, do you feel a buildup or urge that is relieved once you do it?

No, no, there's no buildup or... or urge at all. I know some people get like that, where they just have to do something, but it's really not like that for me. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, losing control or anything like that. 

It's just... I'm just working, trying to be quick for the customers, and then it just happens. There's no warning or feeling beforehand. I just tap the scanner a few times or my hand just stops. And then I'm right back to work. It's really very mild. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture so we can get this little hiccup fixed. I'm really trying my best to be helpful.
Have you had trouble understanding social cues or making back-and-forth conversation since you were a child?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been a little quiet, maybe, but I don't think I've ever had trouble understanding people or talking with them. I've always gotten along fine with my coworkers and customers, you know? I try really hard to be polite and listen well. 

I definitely don't want to give the impression that I'm... antisocial or anything like that. I've always been able to hold a conversation just fine. Is that... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can get this all sorted out.
When the tapping starts, can you stop yourself from doing it for a little while if you really try?

Well, I... I really do try. I promise I do. It's just that I kind of get... stuck. Like I was saying before about why I came in, I just keep getting stuck doing these things that really don't fit the moment. The customer is right there waiting, and I'm just frozen with my hand over the cash drawer, or tapping the scanner in that little pattern. 

If I could just stop it right away, I definitely would, especially since, you know, it got me written up last week. I try so hard to just snap out of it and keep the line moving because I really do want to do a good job. 

Did I explain that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so we can figure this out.
If your attention is pulled to something else, does the tapping or freezing usually stop?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed if something else distracts me enough to make it stop. Usually, when it happens, I'm just so focused on trying to get through the transaction and not keep the customer waiting. 

I mean, the store can get pretty loud, and people are always asking questions or, you know, the phone rings... but I haven't really paid attention to whether that snaps me out of it. I'm sorry, I wish I had a better answer for you. I just really want to give you the exact right information so I'm not leading you down the wrong path. Does that make sense? I can try to pay closer attention next time if that would help you figure this out.
Have you ever had sudden sounds or words come out on their own, like throat-clearing, sniffing, grunting, or blurting something out?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I don't... I don't blurt things out or make weird noises. I try very hard to be professional at the register. I mean, maybe I clear my throat sometimes if it's dry from talking to customers all day, but that's just normal, right? 

I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm standing there grunting at people or anything. I'm always very polite. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how I act at work.
When one of these episodes is happening, if someone suddenly says your name, does it stop right away?

Um, well... like I was mentioning earlier about how I keep getting stuck doing those things at the register? You know, freezing up over the cash drawer or tapping the scanner in that pattern while the customer is waiting... if someone actually says my name, like my manager or a coworker, I think it does stop. Or at least, I try my absolute hardest to snap out of it right that second. 

I really don't want to look like I'm ignoring anybody, especially since I got written up for it last week. I want to be a good employee, so if they call my name, I do my best to jump right back to the transaction. I really hate that I do things that don't fit the moment like that. 

Is... is that a good sign? That I can stop if someone calls my name? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so I can get back on track at work.
When you start paying close attention to the tapping or freezing, does it usually get worse?

Um, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really... experimented with it like that. When it happens, I'm usually just so embarrassed that I'm holding up the line, you know? I just try to push past it as quickly as I can. 

I don't think I've ever just stopped and focused on the tapping or the freezing while it's happening. I'm too busy worrying about what the customer is thinking or if my manager is watching. I just want to do a good job and be normal. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not very helpful. Do you... do you want me to try paying attention to it next time? I can definitely try to do that if you think it's important for figuring this out. I just want to make sure I'm doing whatever you need me to do.
